questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: LUISS has a strong reputation within the field of political science, as well as an innovative learning approach. Furthermore, the rich culture and history of Rome was a crucial variable in my choice of destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed urgent assistance regarding my courses, as unforeseen rescheduling jeopardised my exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was extremely hard. Wouldn't recommend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived with four locals, which added another dimension to my exchange. Thereby, really enriching.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: LUISS accommodation services was really bad and extremely unhelpful.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration is a first come first service system, meaning that the registration is quite stressful. Furthermore, the registration takes place over two periods as the schedule of the courses change drastically from the first to the second.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much to be honest, however Italian administration processes are organised chaos.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fairly successful. Had to give up one course, however got the rest.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to have a lot of courses accepted by KU before going, as courses may not be available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses are in alignment with the level at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching is more "high-school-like" with smaller classes and more access to the professor. Furthermore, you'll do presentation, debates etc. regarding the topics studied in order to support your learning efforts.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The International Relations of the European Union
Comparative Politics
European Neighbourhood Policy and Migration
Crisis Communication 
Corporate Strategy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think "The International Relations of the European Union" and "Comparative Politics" was extremely interesting, and lectured by some of the leading professors in European academia.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food - particularly meat, wheat-products and vegetables - was fairly cheap, as a consequence of diversified VAT. Utilities, particularly gas, is quite expensive though. However, in the current political context I don't think that is an exclusive competence of Italy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is multiple sports teams, parties, trips and political events available for students to participate in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend participating in "the opening week" activities arranged by ESN.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Apart from the obvious, Colosseum, the Vatican, Trevi Fountain etc. I would recommend going to a city just out of Rome called Tivoli, which is really rich in terms of architecture and history.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Drink espresso, and embrace "the aperitivo".

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Less organisation, and a general approach embedded in "building the plane as we fly".

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food is absolutely fantastic.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Start organising housing early - recommend already in February as Rome is extremely hard to find accommodation in.

2. Make sure to have a lot of classes approved by KU-merit, before departure as courses are rescheduled upon until the week before lectures start demanding a certain degree of flexibility.

3. Remember to enjoy yourself. You are going to live in of the most important cities in the history of mankind. Embrace that, and make sure you enjoy the city and all the wonderful people you are going to meet on your way.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect a little bit more chaos in terms of the administrative department at LUISS.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many new wonderful people from diverse cultures and countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To make sure that I got to do all the things I wanted before leaving. Time runs fast when you are having fun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
